confirm.namePinnedHint: Name is kept — refresh does not rename
confirm.errorNameTakenTitle: A dataset with that name already exists in this workspace
confirm.errorNameTakenDescription: Rename one of the items in the table above (the wizard's Confirm step) so each dataset name is unique within this workspace, then try again.
confirm.errorCoercionFailedTitle: Some values don't fit the chosen column type
confirm.errorCoercionFailedDescription: {{column}} can't convert to {{dtype}} — {{count}} value(s) don't fit. Examples: {{samples}}. Nothing was created.
confirm.errorCoercionFailedHint: If the failing values look like real data, the chosen type or format doesn't match them — adjust it on the Metadata step. If they're junk rows (stray text, totals, repeated headers), fix those rows in the source file and re-upload.
confirm.errorCoercionFailedHeaderRowHint: A failing value equals the column name — the file likely contains a repeated header row; delete that row in the source file and re-upload.
confirm.errorCoercionFailedTimeInDateHint: The failing values carry a time part but the chosen type is date — choose datetime instead (e.g. format dd-MM-yyyy HH:mm:ss). To group by day or week, add a Date bucket step in a query afterwards.
confirm.errorMergeDuplicateKeysTitle: The new file repeats the key
confirm.errorMergeDuplicateKeysDescription: {{count}} key value(s) ({{key}}) appear on more than one row in the new file, so merge can't tell which row wins. Examples: {{samples}}. Add another column to the key (e.g. a date) or clean the export, then try again. Nothing was changed.
confirm.errorUnexpectedDescription: The app sent something the server refused — a bug in the app, not something you did. Check the Datasets list before retrying. Details: {{detail}}

refresh.title: Refresh dataset
refresh.subtitle: Re-upload a new export into “{{name}}”.
refresh.sourceBannerBody: Pick the new export file. The workspace, source type, and your previous column settings are carried forward.
refresh.sheetNote: Refresh targets the original sheet “{{sheet}}” — pre-selected.
refresh.sheetNoteMissing: The original sheet “{{sheet}}” isn’t in this file — pick the sheet to update from.
refresh.sheetSelectionHint: Pick exactly one sheet — this update applies to one dataset.
refresh.confirmReplaceBody: Refresh does a whole-table replace — the previous rows are overwritten (no version history). The dataset keeps its name and id, so queries and dashboards built on it stay connected.
refresh.legacyNote: Some settings couldn’t be restored from an older upload — please re-check the column types and format before continuing.
refresh.modeReplaceHint: The new file’s rows replace everything currently in the dataset.
refresh.modeMergeHint: Rows matching on the key are updated from the new file; rows only in the dataset are kept; new keys are added.
refresh.mergeKeyPlaceholder: Pick the column(s) that identify a row
refresh.mergeKeyRequired: Pick at least one key column to merge.
refresh.mergeKeyIssueMissing: “{{name}}” is missing from the new file’s kept columns.
refresh.mergeKeyBlockedTitle: Merge is blocked by the key column(s)
refresh.mergeKeyBlockedHint: Fix the column or its type, pick a different key, or switch to Replace.
refresh.confirmMergeTitle: This merges the new file into “{{name}}”
refresh.confirmMergeBody: Rows sharing the key ({{key}}) are updated from the new file; rows only in the dataset are kept; new keys are added. The dataset keeps its name and id, so queries and dashboards built on it stay connected.
refresh.modeAppendHint: Adds all the new file’s rows and keeps everything already in the dataset. Does not remove duplicates.
refresh.overlapFieldLabel: Check for repeated periods by date (optional)
refresh.overlapFieldPlaceholder: Pick a date column to check — or leave empty
refresh.overlapFieldNone: This file has no date column to check.
refresh.confirmAppendTitle: This adds the new rows to “{{name}}”
refresh.confirmAppendUncheckedBody: Append keeps every row and doesn’t remove duplicates. With no date column to check, we can’t warn you about re-adding a period already in the dataset — appending it again will double those rows.
refresh.overlapChecking: Checking “{{field}}” for dates already in the dataset…
refresh.overlapClean: No overlapping “{{field}}” dates — this adds a new period. Append keeps all rows.
refresh.overlapWarnTitle: These dates are already in the dataset
refresh.overlapWarnBody: The new file’s “{{field}}” overlaps from {{min}} to {{max}}, which “{{name}}” already covers. Appending will add those rows again (duplicates). You can still proceed.
refresh.overlapCheckFailed: Couldn’t check “{{field}}” for overlaps — append will still add all rows.

drift.noneBody: The new file’s columns match the current dataset. Nothing downstream is affected.
drift.title: Schema changes detected
drift.subtitle: The new file’s columns differ from the current dataset. Review the changes below, then acknowledge to continue — a refresh never silently absorbs drift.
drift.removedHint: Present before, missing now — dependent queries or relationships that use these may go stale.
drift.dtypeChangedHint: The current type and the new file’s detected type differ. Your dataset keeps its current type unless you changed it — the new file’s values are converted to match.
drift.addedHint: Present in the new file, not in the current dataset.
drift.blastRadiusStub: A preview of the queries and relationships that reference the removed / changed columns lands with the backend read (later this round). Until then, dependents are flagged automatically the next time they’re opened.
drift.acknowledge: I understand these schema changes and want to continue.
